es.summary: El pramipexol es un agonista de los receptores dopaminérgicos D2/D3 usado como terapia adyuvante en la enfermedad de Parkinson y trastornos extrapiramidales.
key_points: Aumenta la estimulación dopaminérgica en el cerebro, mejorando la motilidad.
Se administra oralmente y se absorbe rápidamente.
Los efectos adversos frecuentes incluyen náuseas, somnolencia y edema periférico.
Puede producir hipotensión ortostática y alucinaciones, que requieren vigilancia.
No debe combinarse con inhibidores de MAO‑B sin supervisión médica.

mechanism: Se une a los receptores D2 y D3 mimetizando la dopamina endógena.
Estimula la vía nigroestriada, mejorando el control motor.
No atraviesa la barrera hematoencefálica como la dopamina exógena.
indications: Enfermedad de Parkinson en fase temprana o como complemento a levodopa.
Trastornos del movimiento inducidos por fármacos neurolepticos (extrapiramidales).
Síndrome de piernas inquietas cuando otras terapias fallan.
adverse_effects: Edema periférico, especialmente en extremidades inferiores.
interactions: Aumenta riesgo de efectos neuropsiquiátricos con antipsicóticos.
Puede intensificar efectos de inhibidores de MAO‑B.
Los antieméticos que bloquean dopamina pueden reducir su eficacia.
nursing_care: Evaluar presión arterial y pulso antes y después de la dosis; retener si PA ortostática <90/60 mmHg.
Monitorear estado mental para detectar alucinaciones o confusión.
Observar signos de edema y registrar peso diariamente.
Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si aparecen náuseas intensas o hipotensión grave.
Documentar respuesta motora y cambios en la capacidad para realizar actividades de la vida diaria.
patient_teaching: Tomar el medicamento con alimentos para reducir náuseas.
Levantarse despacio de la cama o silla para evitar mareos.
Informar al profesional de salud si aparecen alucinaciones, confusión o edema.
Evitar el consumo de alcohol y sedantes que potencien la somnolencia.

outcomes: Seguridad del paciente: sin caídas durante la hospitalización
Control de síntomas: reducción del temblor a nivel leve en 48 h

interventions.action: Evaluar la marcha y el equilibrio antes de la administración y cada 4 h.
interventions.rationale: Detectar deterioro que aumente el riesgo de caídas.

interventions.action: Medir presión arterial en posición supina y de pie antes de cada dosis.
interventions.rationale: Identificar hipotensión ortostática que pueda provocar desmayos.

interventions.action: Mantener el entorno libre de obstáculos y usar barandillas en la cama.
interventions.rationale: Reducir la probabilidad de tropiezos y caídas.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre levantarse lentamente y usar calzado antideslizante.
interventions.rationale: Prevenir mareos y caídas al cambiar de posición.

interventions.action: Reportar al médico cualquier alucinación o confusión nueva.
interventions.rationale: Permitir ajuste de dosis o cambio de terapia para evitar conductas peligrosas.

en.summary: Pramipexole is a D2/D3 dopamine receptor agonist used as adjunct therapy in Parkinson's disease and extrapyramidal disorders.
key_points: Increases dopaminergic stimulation in the brain, improving mobility.
Common adverse effects include nausea, drowsiness, and peripheral edema.
May cause orthostatic hypotension and hallucinations, requiring monitoring.
Should not be combined with MAO‑B inhibitors without medical supervision.

mechanism: Binds to D2 and D3 receptors mimicking endogenous dopamine.
Stimulates the nigrostriatal pathway, improving motor control.
Does not cross the blood‑brain barrier like exogenous dopamine.
indications: Early-stage Parkinson's disease or as a complement to levodopa.
Restless legs syndrome when other therapies fail.
adverse_effects: Peripheral edema, especially in lower extremities.
interactions: Increases risk of neuropsychiatric effects with antipsychotics.
May intensify effects of MAO‑B inhibitors.
Antiemetics that block dopamine can reduce its efficacy.
nursing_care: Assess blood pressure and pulse before and after dose; hold if orthostatic BP <90/60 mmHg.
Monitor mental status for hallucinations or confusion.
Observe for edema and record weight daily.
Hold dose and notify physician if severe nausea or hypotension occurs.
Document motor response and changes in ability to perform activities of daily living.
patient_teaching: Take medication with food to reduce nausea.
Stand up slowly from bed or chair to avoid dizziness.
Inform healthcare provider if hallucinations, confusion, or edema develop.
Avoid alcohol and sedatives that increase drowsiness.

outcomes: Patient safety: no falls during hospitalization
Symptom control: reduction of tremor to mild level within 48 h

interventions.action: Assess gait and balance before administration and every 4 h.
interventions.rationale: Detect deterioration that increases fall risk.

interventions.action: Measure blood pressure in supine and standing positions before each dose.
interventions.rationale: Identify orthostatic hypotension that may cause fainting.

interventions.action: Keep environment free of obstacles and use bed rails.
interventions.rationale: Reduce likelihood of tripping and falls.

interventions.action: Educate patient on rising slowly and using non‑slip footwear.
interventions.rationale: Prevent dizziness and falls when changing position.

interventions.action: Report any new hallucination or confusion to the physician.
interventions.rationale: Allow dose adjustment or therapy change to avoid dangerous behaviors.

sections.mechanism.1.quote: Activating these receptors causes increased dopamine levels in the nigrostriatal pathway, which leads to smooth and coordinated movements.

sections.mechanism.2.quote: Notably, administering exogenous dopamine is not an option because it has difficulty crossing the blood–brain barrier and has an extremely short half-life.

sections.indications.0.quote: Indications Used alone in early-stage PD Combined with levodopa in advanced stages of PD

sections.indications.1.quote: For control of extrapyramidal disorders (except tardive dyskinesia) caused by neuroleptic drugs

sections.adverse_effects.3.quote: Adverse Effects Severe allergic reaction Suicidal thoughts Livedo reticularis Seizures NMS Orthostatic hypotension Tachypnea Anx

sections.adverse_effects.4.quote: In such cases, anti-Parkinsonian drugs can precipitate a toxic psychosis characterized by confusion, memory impairment, visual hallucinations, delusions, and nervousness.

sections.interactions.0.quote: Other antihypertensives can exacerbate orthostatic hypotension.

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: In such cases, anti-Parkinsonian drugs can precipitate a toxic psychosis characterized by confusion, memory impairment, visual hallucinations, delusions, and nervousness.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Move and change positions slowly due to orthostatic hypotension.

sections.patient_teaching.3.quote: Avoid alcohol and sedatives, including over-the-counter medications that contain these.
